elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: "and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf"

elements.element: Paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: "are perpetual and irrevocable to the extent paid-up"

elements.element: Ongoing/subscription rights terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: "may otherwise be terminated only for the Company's uncured material breach"
"are transferable to any successor to the Company's business"

elements.element: Affiliates covered (fallback conditions coverage on written notice)
elements.evidence: "extend to the Company's affiliates" — covered unconditionally, so the notice condition is unnecessary

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "any successor to the Company's business (including in a merger or acquisition)"

reasons: The single appended sentence supplies all five preferred atomic elements: affiliate extension, contractor extension, perpetual-and-irrevocable paid-up rights, termination limited to Customer's uncured material breach, and transferability to successors.

The clause had no licence-scope language at all, so a concise insertion is the minimal fix; the original Section 1.4 text is untouched and no new exception, undefined term, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Fallback is also independently satisfied (affiliates covered; transfer to an M&A successor expressly permitted), but the drafter's locked preferred level is achieved, so no fallback fallback-mixing arises.
